component_findings.async_structured: Recertified level 2 under the current criterion: Asynchronous concurrency has first-class composition and structured lifetime/join/cancellation mechanisms or an equivalent disciplined model. Evidence basis: The Io-based concurrency redesign was still in flux at the evaluated Zig version, so ergonomics and stability of structured async are lower than in languages with a settled concurrency story. | Static language-design analysis based on Zig's std.Thread, std.Io (evolving async I/O abstraction visible in mb09.zig via std.Io.Threaded.init_single_threaded and threaded.io()), and absence of language-level async/await syntax as of the evaluated Zig version. | mb09.zig demonstrates the std.Io abstraction: an explicit Io interface object (threaded.io()) is passed to I/O calls, and std.Io.Threaded.init_single_threaded is used to select a concrete (currently single-threaded) execution strategy -- this shows Zig's concurrency model is being redesigned around an explicit, allocator-like Io capability rather than implicit async keywords. | Zig provides std.Thread for OS threads, std.Thread.Mutex, Condition, RwLock for synchronization primitives, and std.atomic for lock-free primitives, all as ordinary library code with no special compiler magic -- consistent with Zig's no-hidden-control-flow philosophy. | There is no built-in colorless async/await language keyword pipeline stabilized at the evaluated version (Zig's async/await was removed and is being replaced by the Io interface pattern seen above), so structured concurrency and cooperative scheduling are not yet a stable first-class langua…

metric.concurrency.selection_rule: Judge intrinsic concurrency/parallelism semantics and core runtime primitives. External frameworks and debugger/tool maturity are out of scope.

component_findings.abi_calling_control: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: ABI/calling-convention/linkage choices are explicit or safely standardized for common interoperability cases. Evidence basis: C++ name-mangled symbols and templates are not interoperable without an extern C shim, matching common practice in comparable systems languages; this is a design constraint, not unique to Zig. | Static language-design analysis of Zig's C interoperability model, informed by reading assigned micro/adversarial program sources (e.g. mb09.zig using std.heap.c_allocator, std.process.Init.Minimal, std.Io.File for OS-level syscall interfacing) which demonstrate native, zero-wrapper access to C ABI facilities directly from idiomatic Zig code. | Zig can directly @cImport C headers with no binding-generation step and no separate IDL, translating C declarations into native Zig types at compile time. | Zig structs/enums/unions can be declared extern to guarantee C-compatible ABI layout, and functions can be declared export or callconv(.C) to be called from C or to call into C with zero overhead (no marshalling layer, no runtime boxing). | c_allocator (seen used directly in mb09.zig) demonstrates first-class direct use of libc malloc/free as an Allocator, evidencing that Zig treats C interop as a built-in language citizen rather than a bolted-on FFI library. | Zig has no hidden runtime (no GC, no exception unwinding ABI mismatch, no implicit stack frames) so crossing the C boundary requires no runtime shims -- calling convention and layout compatibility is sufficient. | Cross-language safety…
